key_findings.title: DMK: #1 Recipient in Tamil Nadu, #6 Nationally in Electoral Bonds
key_findings.detail: DMK received ₹639.00 Crore through electoral bonds, making it by far the largest recipient in Tamil Nadu and the 6th highest political party in India, ahead of large national parties like AAP (₹65 Cr) and regional parties like JD(U) (₹14 Cr) and SP (₹14 Cr).

key_findings.title: Lottery King Santiago Martin's Future Gaming Alone Gave 78.7% of DMK's Bonds
key_findings.detail: Future Gaming and Hotel Services PR (Santiago Martin), which was under investigation by the Enforcement Directorate, donated ₹503.00 Crore to DMK alone between 2020 and 2024. Megha Engineering (MEIL) was #2 with ₹85.00 Crore.

key_findings.title: AIADMK Encashed All Bonds in Single Window (April 2019)
key_findings.detail: Unlike DMK, AIADMK only encashed electoral bonds during the April 2019 Lok Sabha elections (38 bonds totaling ₹6.05 Crore). AIADMK's primary funding comes from application fees, corpus interest, and general party funds.

key_findings.title: The Principle of Zero: Parties that Stood Against Electoral Bonds
key_findings.detail: CPI(M), CPI, and regional parties like NTK took zero electoral bonds. CPI(M) was the lead petitioner before the Supreme Court of India in Association for Democratic Reforms & CPI(M) v. Union of India, which declared the electoral bond scheme unconstitutional on February 15, 2024.

key_findings.title: NTK's Crowdfunding Model vs Mega-Donors
key_findings.detail: Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) declared ₹3.32 Crore in FY 2024-25, almost entirely powered by micro-contributions aggregated through Cashfree Payments India and individual cadre donations with full PAN declarations.

key_findings.title: TVK: Vijay's Political Entry & High-Value Direct Contributions
key_findings.detail: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), registered with the ECI on 03/09/2024 by actor-politician Vijay, submitted statutory Form 24A reports declaring ₹1.22 Cr in FY 2024-25 (with ₹65.82 Lakh personal cheque from Vijay) and ₹13.30 Cr in FY 2025-26, powered by ₹8.20 Cr via RTGS from Aadhav Arjun and ₹5.00 Cr via RTGS from Ranjith Kumar.

key_findings.title: The Warchest Asymmetry in Tamil Nadu Politics
key_findings.detail: In total reserves, National ruling party BJP holds ₹12,164.15 Crore in General Reserves (with ₹9,996 Crore in bank deposits). DMK holds ₹747.52 Crore (with ₹737.5 Crore in bank deposits), AIADMK holds ₹327.16 Crore, and INC holds ₹365.49 Crore.
